'''Artiodacs'''  were a [[Sentience|sentient]], bipedal species native to the cold, swampy world of [[Artiod Minor]], recognized for their stocky, muscular build. They exhibited slightly hunched postures. Despite a naturally solitary disposition, Artiodacs have a long history of serving in gladiatorial arenas, private armies, and as hired muscle, and they maintain cultural practices such as tending aqua-farms and raising [[Prengalli]]. Notable Artiodacs include [[Strono Tuggs|Strono “Cookie” Tuggs]], a palace chef and mobile diner operator, [[Sorka]], a criminal syndicate member turned investigator, and [[Cykon]], a smuggler and co-pilot.
==Biology and appearance==
Artiodac were a [[Sentience|sentient]] bipedal species with two bulging [[Limb|arms]] and two legs. They had tough hides and deep, rumbling voices<ref name="Aliens of the Galaxy" /> The species had a stocky, muscular build. They had a large, dome-shaped head with a prominent snout, small narrow eyes and small flat ears. A humanoid species, they possessed two [[limb|arms]] ending in four-fingered hands and two legs ending in plantigrade feet. They exhibited a slightly hunched posture with a wide stance.<ref name="Uprising Art">[[The Art of Star Wars: Uprising]]</ref>
==Society and culture==
Although most Artiodacs were quiet, solitary beings by nature, centuries of [[Slavery|enslavement]] forced upon them the reputation of serving as [[gladiator]]s in [[The galaxy|galactic]] arenas, hired muscle for [[crime lord]]s, and janissaries in private armies.<ref name="Aliens of the Galaxy" /> As juveniles, they foraged in scrub forests to gather [[Shuimi]] feathers for mating crowns, while bonded pairs later devoted their long lives to raising schools of [[Prengalli]] on carefully maintained aqua-farms. Mated Artiodacs spent their long lifespans tending to [[aqua-farm]]s on their homeworld, where they cared for schools of [[prengalli]].<ref name="Aliens of the Galaxy" /> Members of the species could live for several [[Standard century|centuries]].<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" />
==History==
Artiodacs were [[Homeworld|native]] to the cold, [[swamp]]y [[planet]] [[Artiod Minor]],<ref name="VE" /> a [[Wild Space]] [[planet]] located in the [[Artiod system]] of the [[Morellian Commonwealth]] region near the [[Corporate Sector]].<ref name="Appendix">{{GalaxyMapAppendix}}</ref> Many Artiodacs were enslaved by the [[Zygerrian Slave Empire]]<ref name="Aliens of the Galaxy" /> who overran Artiod Minor.<ref name="VE" />

Sometime after [[34 ABY]]<ref name="AlienArchiveJournalDate">{{AlienArchiveJournalDate}}</ref>, a journal featuring an illustration of an Artiodac, was exhibited at the [[Graf Archive]] on [[Orchis 2]]<ref name="Alien Archive">''[[Star Wars: Alien Archive]]''</ref>. The illustration was attributed to an [[Unidentified artist|unknown artist]] and was later restored and expanded as part of the [[Graf Archive restoration effort]] during [[Xoddam Lothipp]]’s tenure as [[Deputy Director]] of the archive.<ref name="Alien Archive" />
==Artiodacs in the galaxy==
During the [[High Republic Era]], a muscular and gray-skinned Artiodac was employed as a bouncer at [[Mog’s Cantina]] in [[Barraza City]]’s [[market square]] on [[Eiram]]. The Artiodac oversaw the entrance as patrons entered and left.<ref name="Haunted Starlight">''[[The High Republic: Haunted Starlight]]''</ref> In [[228 BBY]]<ref name="THRContent228BBY">{{THRContent228BBY|TOTN}}</ref> an Artiodac served as a volunteer member of the [[Republic Defense Coalition]] aboard a Republic support vessel orbiting [[Angoth]]. The Artiodac was part of a team of peacekeepers and civilian personnel, deployed to provide logistical support and assist [[Jedi]] operatives during operations against the [[Shrikarai|Nameless]]. They were one of ten RDC personnel who participated in a [[Mission to Angoth|mission]] to capture a Nameless from [[Nihil]] [[Pirate|marauders]]. The Artiodac remained on the ship during offensive actions, ready to act in a support or relief capacity, and was observed by [[Padawan]] [[Amadeo Azzazzo]] among the assembled personnel.<ref name="Tears of the Nameless">''[[The High Republic: Tears of the Nameless]]''</ref>

[[File:Strono Tuggs VD.png|thumb|left|200px|The disfigured cook Strono “Cookie” Tuggs was an Artiodac.]]
A disfigured, Artiodac named [[Strono Tuggs]], known as “Cookie”, had a glowing left eye and worked in the kitchens of [[Maz Kanata]]’s [[Takodana Castle|palace]] on [[Takodana]]. Tuggs avoided discussing his past, and Maz respected his silence, keeping her friend’s secrets<ref name="Strono Tuggs">{{Databank|strono-cookie-tuggs|Strono "Cookie" Tuggs}}</ref> and allowed him to cook for the castles patrons for centuries.<ref name="Alien Archive" /> Tuggs was present at the castle when [[Rey Skywalker|Rey]] and [[Finn]] followed [[Han Solo]] into the castle<ref name="The Force Awakens" /> in [[34 ABY]].<ref name="EP7Date">{{FilmDate|VII}}</ref>

Following the destruction of the castle and the end of his long career there, Tuggs relocated from [[Takodana]] to [[Batuu]] to establish an independent food transport operation. He founded [[Tuggs' Grub]], a mobile diner aboard a modified [[Sienar-Chall Utilipede Transport]], which he used to prepare meals while traveling and to collect rare ingredients from across the galaxy.<ref name="Strono Tuggs DB">{{Databank|strono-cookie-tuggs|Strono "Cookie" Tuggs}}</ref>

[[Kalo Sulman]] was an [[Artiodac]] on [[Sedri Minor]] who cultivated [[Vratixia renanicus|Vratixian barley]]. After a [[Nihil]] attack on a [[Hutt]] [[starship]] transporting barley from Sedri Minor, the [[Jedi Order]] investigated the planet. When the [[Jedi]] [[Ceret]] and [[Sskeer]] arrived, Sulman met with them and made it clear they were not welcome, stating that the Sedri Minor colony was independent of the [[Galactic Republic]].<ref name="THR 2">[[The High Republic (2021) 2|''The High Republic'' (2021) 2]]</ref>

[[File:Sorka.png|thumb|right|200px|An Artiodac female named Sorka.]]
[[The Smuggler]]'s crew included a [[Unidentified Artiodac staff cook|staff cook]] who served the crew during the [[Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="Staff Cook">''[[Star Wars: Uprising]]''—Crew Member: "Staff Cook"</ref> A [[Gender|female]] [[Artiodac]] named [[Sorka]] lived in the [[Anoat sector]] during the Galactic Civil War. Despite her kind disposition, she served for a time in the criminal [[Ivax Syndicate]], helping many individuals avoid the wrath of [[Voras|Voras the Hutt]]. She later joined the [[Data Seekers]], a secret society whose members investigated the sector’s hidden secrets.<ref name="Sorka">''[[Star Wars: Uprising]]''—Crew Member: "Sorka"</ref>

A female Artiodac smuggler named [[Cykon]] operated as the co-pilot and financial partner of an smuggler captain, jointly funding the purchase of the [[YT-1210 light freighter]] ''[[Steelwing]]'' by providing half of the required [[Galactic Credit Standard|credits]]. Despite the vessel’s heavy armament, many of its systems were in poor condition, leading to ongoing tension between the two. Cykon accompanied her partner to [[Delphon City]] in search of work and participated in negotiations with the mercenary droid MC-99, who hired the crew to transport concealed artifacts hidden within [[Lugjack]] gaming machines to [[Cloud City]] on [[Bespin]].<ref name="Smuggler mission">''[[Choose Your Destiny: A Smuggler Mission]]''</ref>

During preparations for the job, the Artiodac assisted in acquiring [[electro-bafflers]] to evade security scans and incapacitated an [[Stormtrooper|Imperial stormtrooper]] during an escape from Delphon City. She helped load the contraband aboard the ''Steelwing'' and piloted the ship despite sustaining damage to its landing gear. Upon arrival at Cloud City, the operation was revealed to have been orchestrated by [[Landonis Balthazar Calrissian|Lando Calrissian]] to expose corruption within Cloud City Security, after which the Artiodac and her partner were allowed to depart, though their payment was confiscated to settle outstanding debts.<ref name="Smuggler mission" />

[[File:KajHitsArtiodac-WOTBH4LOMZuckuss1.png|thumb|left|200px|The Chagrian Kaj hits an Artiodac in the face with a bottle.]]
An Artiodac patron was present in [[Jega's Music Hall and Petting Zoo]] on [[Nar Shaddaa]], where the Artiodac and an [[Ithorian]] companion harassed a [[Chagrian]] [[Gender|female]] named [[Kaj]]. Their actions drew the attention of Kaj’s partner, the [[Lurmen]] [[Trot]], who demanded they stop. The confrontation escalated when Kaj struck the Artiodac with a bottle, triggering a brawl. The Artiodac was ultimately subdued by Kaj and forcibly removed from the cantina by [[Mareesee]].<ref name="WOTBH 4&Z">[[War of the Bounty Hunters – 4-LOM & Zuckuss 1|''War of the Bounty Hunters – 4-LOM & Zuckuss'' 1]]</ref>

In [[5 ABY]]<ref name="5ABYLD">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of ''[[Aftermath: Life Debt]]'' to [[5 ABY]].</ref>, during the [[Battle of Nag Ubdur|conflict]] on [[Nag Ubdur]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]], transplanted Artiodac [[Refugee|refugees]] lived alongside native [[Ubdurian]] and [[Keldar]] populations. They were present during a brutal Imperial offensive targeting the planet’s [[zersium]]-rich terrain, which resulted in widespread destruction of settlements and significant civilian casualties. The refugees’ experiences were documented by [[Queen of the Core Network|Core Network]] journalist [[Tracene Kane]] and her [[Trandoshan]] cameraman [[Lug]], who reported on the fighting between [[New Republic]] and Imperial forces and the impact on both soldiers and civilians.<ref name="Life Debt">''[[Aftermath: Life Debt]]''</ref>
